claims.claim_text_verbatim: We show that a simple alternative, Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD often outperforms OPD in accuracy and efficiency

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across 17 teacher–student pairs ranging from 1.5B to 235B parameters, Semi-OPD outperforms OPD in 14 cases, with up to +13.6% accuracy and 11.4× training speedup.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD beats OPD on 14/17 pairs with up to 13.6% accuracy gain

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further find that the choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student, quantified by an output-token overlap ratio: OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.
claims.claim_summary: OPD is only beneficial over Semi-OPD when initial teacher-student overlap is high

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our deeper investigation suggests that effective distillation requires on-policyness w.r.t. both the student and the teacher.
claims.claim_summary: Effective distillation requires on-policyness relative to both student and teacher

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For misaligned pairs, student rollouts can become increasingly off-policy w.r.t. the teacher as context length grows, weakening the distillation signal.
claims.claim_summary: Misaligned student rollouts drift off-policy from the teacher in long contexts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, Semi-OPD is often more stable, as it distills on shorter contexts while covering full trajectories and exposing the student to more teacher-preferred tokens.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD provides more stable distillation by covering full trajectories on shorter contexts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our Semi-OPD achieves much improved/comparable accuracy for teacher–student pairs with low/high overlap, respectively, while reducing training time by up to 11.4× over OPD.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD matches or improves OPD accuracy while reducing training time by 11.4x

claims.claim_text_verbatim: To answer this, we propose a simple and efficient alternative called semi-on-policy distillation (Semi-OPD), where rollouts are sampled once from the initial student before any training and reused throughout distillation, thus making both rollout and teacher logit generation offline.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD samples rollouts once from the initial student and reuses them offline

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We find that Semi-OPD outperforms OPD on 14 of them, with up to +13.6% accuracy and 11.4× training speedup as shown in Fig. 1, and achieves comparable performance (within a 0.1%–2.6% gap) on the remaining three.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD beats OPD on 14 pairs and remains within 2.6% on three

claims.claim_text_verbatim: OPD is only useful for aligned teacher–student pairs with high overlap in output tokens; for misaligned pairs, Semi-OPD is a better alternative in both accuracy and training efficiency.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD is superior to OPD for misaligned teacher-student pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Effective distillation requires both the on-policyness of training rollout w.r.t. the student and closeness to the teacher; OPD prioritizes the former but may sacrifice the latter.
claims.claim_summary: Distillation requires student on-policyness and teacher closeness, but OPD sacrifices teacher closeness

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Given the target domain and initial teacher–student pair, the choice between OPD and Semi-OPD should be guided by the measured overlap ratio, rather than blindly choosing OPD.
claims.claim_summary: Teacher-student overlap ratio should determine whether to use OPD or Semi-OPD

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Semi-OPD decouples data collection from optimization.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD separates rollout data collection from student optimization

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In addition, rollout generation, teacher scoring, and student optimization are executed as separate phases, each of which can use the full GPU cluster rather than partitioning resources among concurrent student generation, teacher serving, and training.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD executes rollout, scoring, and training in separate full-cluster phases

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We show in Sec. 2.3/ 3 that Semi-OPD outperforms Lightning OPD and that SFT on teacher rollouts has negative effects.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD outperforms Lightning OPD, and pre-distillation teacher SFT hurts performance

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We observe that Semi-OPD outperforms OPD on 14 of 17 pairs with improvements of up to ∼13% over OPD at the last step, and the largest gains are generally achieved on pairs with lower initial overlap.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD yields up to 13% final accuracy improvement over OPD on low-overlap pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the remaining three pairs, Semi-OPD still achieves comparable performance, with gaps of 0.1–2.6%.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD remains within 0.1-2.6% accuracy of OPD on high-overlap pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The difference is especially pronounced for Qwen3 thinking-mode pairs: OPD undergoes a substantial performance collapse during training, whereas Semi-OPD continues to improve.
claims.claim_summary: OPD collapses on Qwen3 thinking pairs while Semi-OPD improves continuously

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We observe that (1) on the Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and Qwen3-4B (non-thinking) students, which have low teacher–student overlap ratios, Semi-OPD outperforms all other baselines in accuracy while also being the most efficient, e.g., achieving +7.1% and +8.8% higher accuracy with 35× and 19.5× less training time than Relay-OPD on the two pairs, respectively, according to Fig. 1 and Tab. 4.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD outperforms all baselines in accuracy and efficiency on low-overlap non-thinking pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: (2) On the Nemotron-Cascade-2 pair, which has a high overlap ratio of approximately 89%, our Semi-OPD remains competitive with other OPD baselines and falls only slightly behind the best baseline by 0.7% accuracy, while reducing the training time by 2.2x as compared to FastOPD and 4.5x compared to OPD.
claims.claim_summary: On high-overlap pairs, Semi-OPD matches top baselines while cutting training time substantially

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The overall accuracy–training-efficiency trade-off is shown in Fig. 1, where Semi-OPD achieves up to an 11.4× speedup over standard OPD and a 2.7× speedup over the fastest baseline, FastOPD.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD achieves up to 11.4x speedup over OPD and 2.7x over FastOPD

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The two quantities are strongly correlated (Pearson’s 𝑟= −0.73 across 17 pairs): pairs with lower initial overlap ratios tend to benefit substantially more from Semi-OPD, while OPD is only needed for pairs with high overlap ratios.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD accuracy gain strongly anti-correlates with initial teacher-student overlap

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 4, we observe that (1) SFT on teacher rollouts slightly increases teacher–student overlap ratios, while Semi-OPD still outperforms OPD on both pairs, albeit by a smaller margin; and (2) Our Semi-OPD without the additional teacher-rollout SFT stage can outperform Semi-OPD with this stage, indicating that SFT on teacher rollouts is unnecessary.
claims.claim_summary: Teacher-rollout SFT before distillation is unnecessary and hurts Semi-OPD performance

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 5(a, b), Semi-OPD consistently outperforms teacher-rollout distillation.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD consistently outperforms distilling directly on teacher-generated rollouts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This indicates that the benefit of Semi-OPD does not come merely from using a fixed rollout cache.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD's advantages do not stem solely from caching offline rollouts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Rather, retaining student-generated trajectories to maintain student on-policyness is also important.
claims.claim_summary: Retaining initial student rollouts preserves crucial student on-policyness during distillation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 6, we vary the rollout length (i.e., the rollout cap) used for OPD training and observe that increasing the rollout cap can hurt the low-overlap pair while benefiting the higher-overlap pair.
claims.claim_summary: Longer OPD rollout caps degrade low-overlap pairs but aid high-overlap pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 5(c, d), restricting supervision to the first quarter substantially slows convergence and reduces final accuracy, whereas training on full trajectories achieves the best peak accuracy.
claims.claim_summary: Distilling on full trajectories outperforms truncating rollouts to early prefixes

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 7, Semi-OPD maintains a larger fraction of such tokens than OPD throughout training.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD maintains a higher percentage of teacher-preferred tokens during training

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Importantly, Semi-OPD also outperforms OPD under top-𝑘reverse KL, as shown in Fig. 8, indicating that its advantage is not specific to the sampled-token objective.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD outperforms OPD under top-k reverse KL as well as sampled-token objective

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 9, on low-overlap pairs, regardless of initialization, all runs eventually converge to the performance level reached by OPD initialized from the initial student model under the same rollout cap, while the warm start only affects the convergence trajectory.
claims.claim_summary: On low-overlap pairs, switching to OPD converges to OPD's baseline equilibrium level

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, for a high-overlap pair, as shown in Fig. 10, switching from Semi-OPD to OPD improves performance and closes most of the gap with OPD applied from scratch.
claims.claim_summary: On high-overlap pairs, switching from Semi-OPD to OPD recovers full OPD accuracy

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Fig. 11, models distilled only on math-heavy datasets [26] also improve on HumanEval and HumanEval+, with Semi-OPD remaining ahead of OPD.
claims.claim_summary: Math-distilled models transfer gains to coding benchmarks, with Semi-OPD outperforming OPD

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This suggests that the gains are not limited to fitting the math training distribution but transfer to broader reasoning tasks.
claims.claim_summary: Distillation gains transfer beyond training domains to broader reasoning tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For example, as shown in Fig. 12, with a base student, the initial rollouts are too weak and Semi-OPD underperforms OPD; with an instruction-tuned student, Semi-OPD regains its advantage.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD requires instruction-tuned student rollouts and underperforms OPD on raw base models

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Thus, Semi-OPD is most suitable when the initial student already produces meaningful trajectories.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD is best suited for initial students capable of meaningful rollouts

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Semi-OPD is faster because rollout generation and teacher scoring are done once before training.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD speeds up training by running rollout generation and scoring once upfront

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For a fixed student, the same rollout cache can also be reused across different teachers; evaluating a new teacher only requires computing its log-probabilities on the cached rollouts.
claims.claim_summary: Semi-OPD rollout caches can be reused across different teacher models without re-generating

claims.claim_text_verbatim: OPD rollouts grow longer and use more self-correction words, eventually exceeding the teacher (dotted), while the frozen rollouts sampled once from the initial student 𝜋0 do not.
claims.claim_summary: OPD rollouts inflate in length and self-corrections, whereas Semi-OPD rollouts remain stable
